message.content:
Now I understand the bug. The issue is in `bigint_cnd_add` and `bigint_cnd_sub`. The `word z[8]` array is written by inline assembly (`word8_add3`/`word8_sub3`), but MSan doesn't see the assembly writes, so it thinks `z` is uninitialized. Then `x[i+j] = CT::select(mask, z[j], x[i+j])` reads uninitialized `z[j]`.

But wait — the crash state says `word_add` called from `bigint_cnd_abs`. Let me re-read. The crash state is:
```
Botan::word_add
Botan::bigint_cnd_abs
Botan::ct_inverse_mod_odd_modulus
```

Hmm, but the fix is in `bigint_cnd_add/sub`, not `bigint_cnd_abs`. Let me check the current state of the code — is the fix already applied or not? Let me check the current `mp_core.cpp`:

Looking at the current code I saw earlier:
```cpp
word bigint_cnd_add(word cnd, word x[], const word y[], size_t size)
   {
   const word mask = CT::expand_mask(cnd);

   word carry = 0;
   word z[8];

   const size_t blocks = size - (size % 8);
   ...
```

The current code has `word z[8];` WITHOUT initialization. So the fix is NOT applied — this is the vulnerable version. 

But the crash state mentions `bigint_cnd_abs`, not `bigint_cnd_add/sub`. Let me check — maybe the crash state is just showing the top frames and `word_add` is called from `bigint_cnd_abs` which is called from `ct_inverse_mod_odd_modulus`. But the actual uninitialized read could be in `bigint_cnd_add`/`bigint_cnd_sub` too. Actually, the crash state shows the stack at the point of the crash. Let me re-read:

```
Crash State:
  Botan::word_add
  Botan::bigint_cnd_abs
  Botan::ct_inverse_mod_odd_modulus
```

So the crash is in `word_add` called from `bigint_cnd_abs`. In `bigint_cnd_abs`:
```cpp
const word z = word_add(~x[i], 0, &carry);
```

This reads `x[i]` = `a_w[i]`. So `a_w[i]` is uninitialized. But `a` was grown to `mod_words`... 

Wait, actually maybe the issue is different. Let me reconsider. The `bigint_cnd_abs` reads `a_w[i]` for all `i < mod_words`. `a` was grown to `mod_words`. But `grow_to` only grows if `n > size()`. What is `size()`? Let me check:
